title: A gym owner can show another gym's logo as their own, and no test checks it
what: When an owner saves the gym's look, the server only checks that the logo sits in the shared logo store. It does not check that the logo was uploaded by this gym, so an owner can point their member app at another gym's logo. The database tests try only a made-up upload ticket; none tries a second gym. Gym web page photos already have this check and a test.
expected: A gym can only use a logo it uploaded itself, and a test proves another gym's logo is refused.
how_often: only if an owner copies another gym's logo link
fix_line: Remember which gym each upload ticket belongs to and accept only that gym's logos; add a second-gym test

title: Anyone with a member app account can create any number of empty gyms
what: An old gym-creation step from the first version of the admin app is still switched on for every signed-in account. The admin app no longer uses it (that screen is kept on disk only), but any member app account can still call it as often as it likes, with no limit and no name check. Each call also turns that account into the owner of the new empty gym, taking it out of its real gym.
expected: Gyms are created only through today's sign-up and HQ paths, with their limits; the old step is switched off.
how_often: only if someone calls it on purpose
fix_line: Take the old create-gym step away from signed-in accounts, or remove it

title: No test proves another gym's owner cannot read this gym's member sign-in profiles
what: The read rule on member sign-in profiles lets a gym's owner or trainer read the profiles of their own gym. The access test checks that a member cannot raise their own role, but never tries an owner of a second gym reading the first gym's profiles. The workout summaries next to it do have that test.
expected: A test signs in as another gym's owner and proves no profile of this gym comes back.
how_often: no known case; a gap in the safety net
fix_line: Add one row to the access test: another gym's owner reads this gym's profiles and gets none

items.reason: The area calls six database functions, all open to the public app key and each working out the gym from the sign-in key: gym details and the web page read (owner or desk key; the page says whether this key may edit), and saving the look, getting a logo upload ticket, saving the web page and getting a page-photo slot (owner key only; a desk key gets OWNER_ONLY). Files go straight into two picture stores, guarded by the ticket or slot. Two Worker addresses: crash reports and the on/off switches, judged in the server areas. The old first-version dashboard still calls a gym-creation step open to every signed-in account: finding 02.

Gyms row (look saved here): one read rule by own gym; the access matrix proves another gym's owner reads none and cannot change the look. Web pages, page-photo slots and logo tickets: row security on with no rule, so apps cannot read them; 0080 test 5 (another gym cannot take the address), 0082 tests 3othergym and 4borrow. Logo store and tickets: only a made-up ticket is tried (finding 01). Member summaries: the matrix proves another gym's owner sees none. Sign-in profiles: no other-gym read test (finding 03).
Rule applied: the logo store and upload tickets, and sign-in profiles, have no other-gym test.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only code, catalog and test files were read.
No key pattern hit in this area. The only key in the code is the public app key, which is meant to ship; no secret or service key.
No AI or paid key in this area; the public app key only reaches the guarded functions.

The area keeps the sign-in in the browser with no end date; the panel sign-in never running out is already open. PIN reset and wrong-try limits are not in this area. The old email sign-in screen is no longer shown.

Text boxes here: colours (server accepts only a 6-digit colour), web page words, area, city, photo captions and map link (server checks length, no links in captions, Google-only map link; the page escapes every word). The page preview runs in a frame with scripts off.

Logo upload: shrunk to PNG in the browser; the server store takes PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 1 MB under a 15-minute ticket, and the ticket can be reused for many files (already open). Page photos: WebP only in this gym's own folder, 12 open slots at most; anyone can list every gym's page photos (already open). Logo not tied to the gym: finding 01.

Logo links sit in a 48-character random folder; page photo names are random. The gym web page address is public by design; the join code shown on this screen and on the public page can be guessed or read, both already open.
Code here uses react, the database library and the shared theme at run time; no alert names them. Vite alerts are build tools only.
